plan: This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction, where bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their behavior. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding exactly my value of $32 ensures I win whenever profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay. Deviating from truthful bidding only reduces expected profit. Therefore, I will bid my true value.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid (not their own bid), there's no incentive to shade my bid up or down—bidding above value risks winning and overpaying, while bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior round history to adjust for, I'll bid exactly my value of $9 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values, bidding one's true value is a weakly dominant strategy: you win exactly when your value exceeds the second-highest bid, and you pay that second-highest bid regardless of your own bid (as long as you're highest). Overbidding risks paying more than value; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With value $46, the optimal action is to bid truthfully at $46, maximizing expected profit given the auction's incentive structure.
